titleEn: It Is All Right to Cry, Then Try Again!

pages.text: "I will decorate this whole playhouse!" Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, hugged an armful of yellow leaves. Beside Teacher Bau sweeping the yard, Mio climbed the ladder.
Impatient Bobo offered leaves. "Stick these on too!" Mio gripped both purple bag straps. "I will make the whole window border yellow."
Mio's arms were full of leaves. Carrying everything alone made them heavy. Halfway up the ladder, Mio jumped down. Thump!
A red scrape crossed a knee. Sting! Leaves scattered across the yard, and Mio's eyes filled with tears. But Mio bit their lip. "It does not hurt. I can do it myself."
When Mio crouched to gather leaves, the knee throbbed. Limping, Mio could not collect even one. Teacher Bau set down the broom and came over.
Teacher Bau sat beside Mio. "Mio, you may say it hurts when it hurts." The tears Mio had held back burst out. "Waaah!"
Teacher Bau hugged Mio and put on a bandage. "It is all right to cry, then try again!" After crying for a while, Mio's chest felt clear.
At the playhouse window, Mio and Bobo stuck leaves side by side. Bobo passed them; Mio pressed them on. Teacher Bau held the ladder. Yellow filled the window border.
The next day, Mio held out a scratched hand. "Teacher, this hurts! One, say it hurts! Two, do not hold back tears! Three, bandage on, then try again!"
Teacher Bau wrapped both arms around Mio and stroked their back. Crying brought strength to try again. Looking at the yellow window, Mio said, "It is all right to cry, then try again!"
